chapter: Rising in Manhattan: clubs, Hilda and the Latin scene
title: La Conga in 1942 and how Tito Puente joined
summary: Puente, a teenager, played with Siboney, was recommended by Mario to Sacasas, then joined Machito for a year and a half.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Okay, Macho, when did you get the job at La Conga?
Nineteen forty-two. Was Tito Puente in the band already?
Okay. How did Puente get into the band?

Well, when we worked at the Beachcomber, Sacasas got here with Miguelito, They had in mind to organize a band, both, but some kind of, I don't know, Miguelito always was, he want to be by himself, he don't want to take order from anybody, so ahh, and Sacasas had the same idea,

so Mario was the interpreter; Mario was the Bauza interpreter with William Morris for Miguelito Valdes and Sacasas. When Sacasas went to Ben Matthews' Riviera, Tito Puente played about two or three nights with us, with the Orquesta Siboney at Brick House, in forty-six between Sixth and Seventh, and he was about fourteen years old.
What was he playing, trap drums or timbales?

......and he was good, so we had an idea, I had an idea the way he played so one day Sacasas want to organize his band and Mario recommend Tito Puente to Sacasas so rather they went to Ben Matthews' Riviera, he went to Chicago with Tito Puente. When they come back, I don't what happened that he quit and Tito Puente came with us and played about one year and a half or two years.
Okay. In 1941 is when he joined the band, right?
